woodsy: Of, relating to, or suggestive of a wooded area.
Of a place: having many trees.
woodwind: Any (typically wooden) musical instrument that produces sound by the player blowing into it, through a reed, or across an opening. Woodwind instruments include the recorder, flute, piccolo, clarinet, oboe, cor anglais and bassoon.
woodwind instrument: A musical instrument in which sound is produced by blowing against an edge or by vibrating a thin piece of wood or metal known as the reed, and in which the pitch is governed by the resonant frequencies of an enclosed air column.
woodwork: Something made from wood, especially cabinets and trim (e.g., baseboards, doorframes) made from millwork.
A place of concealment or obscurity.
The frame of the goal, i.e. the goalpost or crossbar.
woodworking: The crafts of carpentry, cabinet making and related skills of making things from wood.
woodworm: Any of many beetle larvae that bore into wood.
A shipworm, a worm-like mollusk in the family Teredinidae that feeds on wood underwater in saltwater.
woody: Consisting of wood; resembling wood in appearance or texture.
woody island: An island of the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea administered under Sansha, Hainan, China (claimed by Taiwan (ROC) and Vietnam).
woof: The set of yarns carried by the shuttle of a loom which are placed crosswise at right angles to and interlaced with the warp; the weft.
A woven fabric; also, the texture of a fabric.
Something which is interwoven with another thing.
An underlying foundation or structure of something; a fabric.
